newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says lost contact with troops in Yei.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says lost contact with troops in Yei.

text.p: The Sudanese army said on Saturday it had lost contact with its units in the southern town of Yei despite repelling four rebel attacks on the town.
The rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) said it captured Yei on Wednesday but on Friday a cabinet minister in Khartoum said the town was still in government hands.

On Saturday the government spokesman, Culture and Information Minister Tayeb Ibrahim Mohamed Khair, said: "Our forces had been in constant contact with the command but in the past hours there has been no communication for some time."
The minister, in a statement to the official news agency SUNA, said government troops had earlier driven back the four attacks on the town, 1,270 km (790 miles) south of Khartoum.
The Sudanese government says Ugandan troops have been fighting alongside the rebels and Brigadier Khair said on Saturday that their military hardware was proof of foreign help.

"They have amassed large quantities of advanced weapons, heavy artillery and tanks in a way that shows the scale of the military assistance Uganda and its rebel agents have received for carrying out the attack on Sudan," he said.
